** **

**TLDR:** Earnings have been mixed to slightly better heading into the
midterms, Middle East events and funding flows this week. The velocity of
these moves are meaningful and I think we’re in for another week of heightened
volatility. **GOOGL** feedback is negative (not surprising) but their Search
issue is a monetization problem, not a user engagement / ramp issue – it’s a
show me story but Gemini positioning is better now than at any point in the
past year. Despite the broader market malaise,
**MSFT/AMZN/SNDK/KLAC/TXN/STX/EBAY/ETSY all saw notable EPS revisions higher
last week.** As we head into another busy week of earnings the fundamental
setups feel solid for **SHOP/LYV/W** while **Apple** is still viewed as a
relatively safe trade despite EPS estimates likely revising lower given iPhone
sales + margin pressure. Conviction in **DDOG/NET** is lower given the recent
moves across smidcap software and overall funding flows. **DKNG** implied move
on EPS is 8% and with expectations on the floor combined with momentum for
higher margin DkEX + World Cup onboarding, the optionality for EBITDA Guide to
exceed the bear case is compelling.

  

**Thoughts into earnings this week:**



**AAPL (=):** iPhone units will optically look weak, gross margins will be
soft, yet my conviction level in the short thesis has dissipated over the past
couple of days as the market rotates into AI defensive names. While most
shorter duration investors that I spoke with over the past few weeks were
short Apple on higher memory prices / weaker iPhone sales weighing on their
guidance trajectory, the stock has quietly made new all-time highs – in fact
it now exceeds NVDA in market cap heading into the print this week. Newman
noted last week that _“Global iPhone shipment growth slowed to 2% YoY in CQ3
2026, vs. 5% last quarter and 12% in CQ3 2025, driven by September unit
decline of 9% YoY (sell thru), which marked an end to Apple’s18-month streak
of YoY unit growth. This was mostly due to Apple’s delayed launch of the
iPhone 18 base model to spring 2027.”_ As a result, iPhone sales are trending
below the Street this quarter while gross margin downside remains likely –
Newman is modeling 40.4% iPhone gross margin (390bps below cons.), 46.2% Apple
gross margin (50bps below cons.), and $2.87 EPS (1.3% below cons.).
**Fundamentally I would skew short into the print, but given the relative safe
haven trade, it wouldn’t be surprising if narratives outweigh lower EPS
revisions this print.   **

** **

**DDOG (+ -):** Peter recently upgraded
DDOG
to Outperform on continued tailwinds from frontier labs while Muse/Instinct
adds incremental upside as infra requirements scale with adoption. Heading
into last quarter, AI labs were in a lull, though alt data signals enterprise
token consumptions appears to have grown at least 50% QoQ among the frontier
AI cohort. Agentic AI adoption from Muse / Dots adds another lift that Peter
wasn’t previously factoring in. He now models $4 in EPS for FY27 vs Street at
$3.15. **My sense is that sentiment for software has deteriorated this quarter
as the AI hype surrounding the sector fades. While DDOG is a beneficiary of
ongoing adoption of horizontal agents, my sense is this is increasingly priced
into the stock here with expectations remaining high into the print, the setup
feels less compelling given the noise this week and around funding flows
across tech.**

AMD (EW, reporting after the market close on Tuesday, November 3rd): Expect
very strong server CPU to at least compensate for PC headwinds. Following
Intel's surprisingly negative outlook in PCs, and server CPU supply challenges
we see a slightly lower bar for AMD's earnings next week; however it is our
sense that AMD can successfully navigate those challenges - with the caveat
that PC weakness is somewhat unavoidable as the unit TAM continues to shrink.
We cut our client segment estimates from 1.9% q/q growth in Q3 to a 0.3%
decline, and in Q4/Q1 we cut from -3.9%/-10.7% to -7.1%/-13.1%. For FY27 we
now model a 7.3% decline vs 3% growth prior. AMD stock was down >10% on Friday
following INTC's Q3 results, but with PCs moving below 20% of revenue in Q4 if
the company can reiterate its confidence in hitting its datacenter targets
next year we expect shares to regain lost ground.

We feel good about AMD's ability to gain server share even with leading edge
wafer and substrate constraints, and supply chain inputs point to significant
upside to our forecasts for next year. Given the challenges Intel is seeing
with server units up just 4% y/y through the first 9 months of 2026 we think
its a somewhat poor read for AMD, as their planning has likely been targeting
much more robust growth even through the tighter supply environment.AMD has
the benefit of being able to build products customers would prefer vs Intel on
basically any single digit node, and their chiplet approach also gives them
more flexibility to leverage outside additional foundries longer term,
underutilized nodes for less critical tiles, and migrate wafers away from PCs.
Looking at venice the compute tiles are on TSMC 2nm, but the IO dies making up
40% of the silicon area are on N6, with potential variability depending on the
skew
(link). Our greater china semis team currently estimates
4.4mn venice units next year, vs 1mn this year, implying just 15% unit growth
elsewhere on our current forecasts. Depending on the price point for venice,
it could make up a very large share of the $30bn or so in server revenue AMD
guided for 2027. Venice was the first HPC product in volume on TSMC 2nm, and
we think the two companies will continue to work together to optimize its
supply. TSMC has 20 fabs in construction worldwide, a significant level of
scale, and we expect AMD to more than participate in that level of growth.
Substrates are more difficult to have visibility into, but when it comes to
the 70% y/y server growth guidance we know managements outlook was given with
supply in mind.

Despite our enthusiasm for server, GPU is a much larger swing factor in longer
term earnings power vs the server business, and we remain somewhat skeptical.
While AMD's position in GPU is improved, but is still subject to risks near
term with the first volume rackscale deployments having yet to take place
(something we still hear is a challenge in our checks), competition from
Nvidia/ASICs, and the same market anxieties that have pressured the multiples
of NVDA and AVGO. We think our GPU revenue estimate for next year is
conservative at $38bn, implying 2.5GW or so of deployments vs possible
ambitions for 1GW at each of the lead customers next year. However, given
warrant issuance that could cover any incremental GPU profits we would caveat
that growth. In terms of the quarter itself we expect AMD to have no issues
hitting numbers, we model $3.3bn DC GPU revs in Q3 and $6.3bn in Q4 as they
recognize revenue at the ODM level vs when customers accept final delivery.

Changes to Estimates: We are cutting our client CPU estimates both this year
and next, which is slightly more than offset by the incremental strength in
server CPU. We leave our datacenter GPU estimates unchanged. For the full
FY26, we now forecast $51.334bn in revenue, 55.7% non-GAAP gross margins, and
$7.70 in non-GAAP EPS, vs our prior $51.147bn/55.8%/$7.67. For FY27, we
forecast 73.6% topline growth, now looking for $89.134bn in revenue, 55.4%
non-GAAP gross margins, and $15.64 in non-GAAP EPS vs our prior
$88.987bn/55.3%/$15.54. Upward revisions are concentrated in the datacenter
segment, where we now model server revenue y/y growth of 88%/79% in FY26/27 vs
82%/75% previously.

Changes to PT: Our PT of $465 was based on 31x our prior FY27 MW EPS of
$15.09, implying 20x our FY28 EPS estimate. We are rolling our target year to
2028, and raising our multiple assumption slightly to ~22x based on a higher
level of conviction in strong multiyear server CPU growth. 22x represents a
premium to AI semis NVDA/AVGO but a discount to INTC given lower operating
leverage potential. That brings the target to $510.

\---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

NVTS (UW, reporting after the market close on Tuesday, November 3rd):Guidance
and visibility toward a 2027 ramp for high-power revenue. With mobile expected
to be virtually negligible as a % of revenue by the end of 2026 and already
representing a minority of revenue last quarter, we expect this transition to
remain on track. Longer-term, the focus is on 800V-driven high-power growth,

pushes out the primary GaN content opportunity. Infineon’s recently announced

# Marvell (Neutral)

### More questions than answers

Recent media reports about Marvell’s potential acquisition of Lumentum have caught the market off guard. The strategic fit is strong, but the reported terms – all stock, limited premium – raise questions for both shareholder bases. Consensus forecasts imply EPS dilution for Marvell. For Lumentum, a limited premium is difficult to reconcile with management’s bullishness about the copper-to-optics migration. Strategic complementarity is an insufficient explanation. Both sets of shareholders will need a convincing case for why a combined Marvell-Lumentum entity would be worth more than the two standalone franchises.**Read Full Report **Mike Harrison +44 20 7000 2079 | Mike.Harrison@rothschildandco.com   | Copyright © Rothschild & Co Global Markets Solutions Limited Unsubscribe

Yesterday afternoon I shared the following summary of investor
thoughts/feedback on the Bloomberg report; there are some things here you can
pick holes in, but I’m sharing by way of feedback from >25 investors. Overall
it does feel like people expect some sort of deal, but the price the market is
implying doesn’t make sense to many people. Would love to hear your
thoughts/feedback…



  * Clients assign a high probability to the news of discussions being true (several underlined Ryan Gould on the byline enhances the credibility). 
  * Ppl telling me they view the market reaction as pricing in a deal for MRVL, but less so for LITE (and the pullback in LITE shares this morning was puzzling vis-a-vis an earlier expectation that LITE management may demand a premium). Bears are saying that the market is worried this is a signal of a laser market peak; bulls that ultimately LITE will need a huge premium to be convinced to sell if they’re sold out through 2029. 
  * The ARB VIEW from our Arb Spec Neetu Jhamb: Bloomberg is reporting the deal as all stock. If we use yesterday’s unaffected prices and a premium range of 25%-40%, that gets us to exchange ratio range of 4.54-5.08.  We assume a 12-15 month timeline for the deal given China/antitrust approvals.  I’d expect it to trade at a 65-70% implied probability of closing.  This translates to a gross spread of 8-10% depending on the prices at announcement. Current prices for LITE and MRVL are implying a ~30% premium. _Me: put another way, Arbs say the deal is priced in at a ~30% premium._
  * Clients broadly view this as MRVL doubling down on "optics-everywhere" / scale-in, in conjunction with its Celestial acquisition. One client frames it as binary on a five-year view: "this either looks like an amazing decision, or it marks the top." Several clients see MRVL as leveraging such a deal for all-in bet on CPO/NPO. The read is that UHP laser modules for ELS will gate which players can compete in next-gen optics, and MRVL is currently seen as behind AVGO & NVDA — making this acquisition as much a CPO/NPO positioning move as a components play.__
  * The most-debated question across the desk: why would LITE sell now? Clients note LITE is sold-out through 2029, growing 40–60% with potential to accelerate further if lasers remain the bottleneck, and — unlike prior cycles — laser ASPs have not crashed on the lagging node.__
  * Deal size and dilution are the second major concern. The price tag is large, and near-term EPS dilution might be material against MRVL's own ambitious out-year guidance. One client called this a "career-defining swing" for Matt Murphy's M&A track record – contingent on AI spending growth continuing.__
  * Anti-trust risk is flagged as a real possibility if optics adoption scales to the level bulls expect. Clients include the world's largest, most powerful tech companies, so pushback might not come from regulators acting alone.__
  * The folks expressing concern this points to a sector peak highlight weakness at Eopeolink & Innolight, and others that both COHR and LITE now have financial managements (“Hurlston beat Anderson to the exit.”).__
  * Could there be a third party? Maybe GOOG (diversification away from AVGO) or NVDA (check MRVL, or alternatively keep MRVL independent)__
  * Most respondents pushed back against my COHR comment, and largely view as a loser. Some just don't like COHR's TRx business at all (v. Chinese competitors and even AAOI), many still don’t believe they can execute on 6” wafer, and bears think their OCS technology underperformed. A few did agree, pointing to a merged MRVL-LITE being viewed as unstoppable versus COHR, leading the company to engage in its own M&A, and also setting off a scramble for buyers to find other sources.__

**AAPL (=):** iPhone units will optically look weak, gross margins will be
soft, yet my conviction level in the short thesis has dissipated over the past
couple of days as the market rotates into AI defensive names. While most
shorter duration investors that I spoke with over the past few weeks were
short Apple on higher memory prices / weaker iPhone sales weighing on their
guidance trajectory, the stock has quietly made new all-time highs – in fact
it now exceeds NVDA in market cap heading into the print this week. Newman
noted last week that _“Global iPhone shipment growth slowed to 2% YoY in CQ3
2026, vs. 5% last quarter and 12% in CQ3 2025, driven by September unit
decline of 9% YoY (sell thru), which marked an end to Apple’s18-month streak
of YoY unit growth. This was mostly due to Apple’s delayed launch of the
iPhone 18 base model to spring 2027.”_ As a result, iPhone sales are trending
below the Street this quarter while gross margin downside remains likely –
Newman is modeling 40.4% iPhone gross margin (390bps below cons.), 46.2% Apple
gross margin (50bps below cons.), and $2.87 EPS (1.3% below cons.).
**Fundamentally I would skew short into the print, but given the relative safe
haven trade, it wouldn’t be surprising if narratives outweigh lower EPS
revisions this print.   **

** **

**DDOG (+ -):** Peter recently upgraded
DDOG
to Outperform on continued tailwinds from frontier labs while Muse/Instinct
adds incremental upside as infra requirements scale with adoption. Heading
into last quarter, AI labs were in a lull, though alt data signals enterprise
token consumptions appears to have grown at least 50% QoQ among the frontier
AI cohort. Agentic AI adoption from Muse / Dots adds another lift that Peter
wasn’t previously factoring in. He now models $4 in EPS for FY27 vs Street at
$3.15. **My sense is that sentiment for software has deteriorated this quarter
as the AI hype surrounding the sector fades. While DDOG is a beneficiary of
ongoing adoption of horizontal agents, my sense is this is increasingly priced
into the stock here with expectations remaining high into the print, the setup
feels less compelling given the noise this week and around funding flows
across tech.**



**UBER (+ -)** : Not much incremental heading into the print. The AV debate
remains front and center and the longer we go without removing the safety
driver, the worse the narrative will get. Right now I think sentiment is
neutral to slightly worsening primarily on Tesla’s ramp in Texas. AV timing
matters and management expects to have 15 cities live with AV deployments by
YE26 (including 6 US) with battleground cities including the Bay Area, London
and Tokyo, but this remains a show me story. I’ll be listening for incremental
details around Nuro, Zoox and Wayve in these cities. I’m hearing the bogie for
3Q Mobility is $29.9B (in line with sell side) and total EBITDA of $2.95B. My
$0.02 is that 3Q should be a relatively uneventful print on in-line Mobility /
EBITDA results given the stock now trades at trough multiples of 11x. Any
signal of them removing the safety driver by year end 2026 should be the
positive catalyst the bulls have been waiting for. And if it’s more likely a
1H27 event, I think longer duration investors would be relatively OK with that
outcome.



**SHOP (= +)** : While expects have risen in recent weeks (I’m hearing 32% GMV
growth in my conversations for 3Q), quantifying de-minimis impact is
percolating in my chats. Even through the 3Q noise, I still view the 4Q setup
as compelling with recent product roadmap around Sidekick/App UI and easier
comps. Management brought Sidekick lower down funnel to checkout and updated
their App UI for merchants in the past couple weeks, which bodes well for
continued adoption and GMV momentum. The bulls are looking for accelerating
GMV growth guide, though FCF margins given these investments are being
debated. **Overall, I think GMV is the primary focus and if the guide calls
for acceleration look for a +ve reaction from momentum traders on the AI
narrative – ecommerce trends have been largely positive from Amazon, eBay and
Etsy while takeaways from payments platforms suggest strong consumer spending
trends into 4Q. Overall the setup feels good here.**  



**LYV (+)** : **A compelling setup into 3Q and through 1H27. In general, top-
line is accelerating into year end, while the touring pipeline suggests
continued growth momentum in 1H. They will begin to benefit from prior venue
nation investment (+ve for AOI margin expansion next year).**   Secular
tailwinds continue for live events, and top line is poised to accelerate for
3Q/4Q. Looking ahead, 1H27 momentum is building with strength across both
established headliners and a growing cohort of artists moving into larger
venues. Venue Nation is entering a period where prior investments will begin
to inflect positive for the company. The company offered deferred revenue
disclosure post 2Q print which supports the +ve setup into earnings this week.
For the quarter, margin expansion should accelerate relative to last year
(170bps QoQ vs 80bps last year). Overall, top-line momentum, AOI improvements
and a relative safety trade from AI (ticketmaster is integrated with Muse,
btw) feels like a long into the print (spec sales view).



**OTAs (+ -)** : Sentiment is +ve for ABNB given their vertical AI integration
rather than inking partnerships with agentic platforms and relative
positioning for rev/EPS upside. For ABNB, I’m hearing 3Q 149M/$26.4B/$2.4B for
RMs/GBs/EBITDA. For BKNG/EXPE sentiment is worsening on renewed AI disruption
debates – hearing 3Q RN/GBs for both of 340M/$52.7B and 112M/$32.7B.   ** **



**W** **(=):** I pitched W as my sneaky long in January. Fundamentally, this
is playing out well, with the Middle East as the notable overhang to my bull
case. The stock effectively closed the gap with its post 2Q EPS high as the
market gained comfort in their top-line momentum. That said, with the 4Q bogie
rising to 10% into the print and the stock effectively pricing in ongoing top-
line acceleration, the setup feels tricky. In terms of positioning, I think
the market is leaning long into the print. While they don’t guide to specific
growth rates, we’ll need commentary on acceleration for the bull case to gain
steam on earnings.



**NET (+ -)** : Another interesting setup into the print. Fundamentally, the
numbers look strong particularly on incremental AI tailwinds from their
serverless application platform. Peter recently noted that AI coding agents
are increasingly recommending the product but he thinks the pace of
incremental Cloud Native workloads going into production slowed in early
summer as a result of the “Tokenmaxxing” hangover and again early fall due to
“Patchmageddon” distraction. In all, he lowered 4Q by $20M given the
headwinds, though the stock is down about 15% in the past week, which is
pricing some of this in. Given the overhang within smidcap software right now,
I think most are on the sidelines here with a short skew.



**DKNG (= +)** :**** Beaten down but not broken. In fact, PMs and perps are
incremental and the market is attributing no benefits from these secular
tailwinds to the stock. Elevated CAC spending is priced in here, and the
result should be better than expected EBITDA guidance for FY26 – bears have
been telling me $550M at the low end of the guide. That said, DkEx ramp has
been impressive (high margin) and this gives management optionality to invest
or let a portion of the volume flow through to EBITDA. Not to mention, user
onboarding from the WC was meaningful, another lever that feels
underappreciated to me by the market heading into the print.**Expectations are
very low after Jason’s lackluster showing at conferences in September, though
optionality with PMs flowing through high margin exchange biz feels like the
fundamentals will supersede the narrative for this stock**.



**Who won the click?******



  * Google 3Q26: Is there anything to get excited about?
  * Sandisk FQ1'27: Pricing and buybacks more than offset cost headwinds; Increase est, Reiterate Outperform TP $3000
  * U.S. Tech Hardware/Semis/Networking: How crowded are hardware and semis as we enter H2'26?
  * SpaceX: Update and raise target to $268 - Terrestrial AI build and enterprise broadband add to Orbital AI thesis; Outperform
  * Microsoft 1Q27: Rock solid growth with more to come
  * NFLX tech blog

We upgrade shares of CRWD to Buy from Hold and raise our DCF-derived TP to
$300 as we believe investors are still not fully appreciating the extent to
which AI will expand the market for cybersecurity and CrowdStrike's leadership
at the forefront. We increasingly believe the company's $565bn TAM (CY34)
provided at Fal.Con will prove conservative given a tsunami of cyber demand
materializing as the AI frontier advances. Not all cyber companies will
participate, and we contend those most obviously levered to AI warrant a
substantial premium, just as seen with others in our coverage like PLTR and
SNOW. We contend that in the words of a popular song from the 1970's, "you
ain't seen nothing yet" as the
best is yet to come.We see CRWD's role as a trusted consolidator, endpoint
leader, and its proximity to the token stream all driving outsized value
capture in the AI era. Even with its consolidation success to date, the
company still only possesses MSD % market share and we expect AI will serve as
a consolidation accelerant for the foreseeable future as this still-emerging
technology and its risks become better understood. Further, we see CRWD's
undisputed leadership in endpoint as a distinct advantage reflected in several
recent quarters of core acceleration, given this is where AI happens whether
physical, virtual, agentic, etc. An environment that increasingly values
endpoint visibility and control should ultimately tilt data gravity further
towards the Falcon platform and accelerate the company's powerful flywheel. As
for the token stream, we believe CRWD's product articulation (notably Guardian
and SafeMind), talent (i.e. AI Chief Bartley Richardson), architectural
placement, and partnerships (i.e. Nvidia, CoreWeave), set up well for the
future ahead. _Altogether, we see AI-accelerated TAM growth and compounding
consolidation tailwinds enabling the company to achieve its stated FY30 ARR
target ($10bn) comfortably ahead of schedule and driving compounded growth
>20% for many years to come._From a checks perspective, CrowdStrike's
positioning in the field has never seemed stronger with multiple customers
highlighting the company's advantages as we enter the AI era; the Falcon
platform concurrently offers best-of-breed functionality with best-of-suite
integration, while the single agent architecture and Falcon Flex make deeper
adoption seamless. Therefore, as customers address pressing needs across their
security stacks, CRWD is often cited as the first port of call. Altogether
this ultimately has enabled the company to convert value into dollars notably
faster than many peers. This is most evident in CRWD's accelerating endpoint
momentum for four consecutive quarters (unlike key EDR competitors) amid
broader infrastructure modernization projects as customers race to harden
their defenses against AI-powered adversaries. Our fieldwork points to
sustained momentum for the foreseeable future with many customers highlighting
CRWD as a security partner of choice to guide them through their AI adoption
journeys. In short, our conversations from the field leave us confident in
ample runway to continue taking share at scale in a market poised for massive
growth.As for valuation, we appreciate the premium multiple at which CRWD
trades on near-term fundamentals and the volatility this can imply on the way
to achieving $20bn in ARR and beyond. Our target price is rooted in a longer-
term DCF framework that reflects the sustained value capture we expect the
company to deliver in the new AI paradigm. Said differently, while the market
has been quick to identify and reward AI winners, we think it is still
underpricing the durability of growth and estimate revisions ahead, and a
future where the value of Cyber may ironically prove greater than the entirety
of what it classically protected. We recognize we are showing up late to a
party that's in full swing, but are convinced the best is yet to come._Click

Big-4 Cloud Review: Growth accelerates, backlog expands, more capex coming in
‘27  
---  
| Industry Overview

| Equity   |   01 November 2026  
---  
---  
---  
---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * 3Q Cloud Review: industry growth accelerated 6ppts q/q to 56%, above our 52% est., with GCP & Azure driving most upside.
  * Sector Backlog/RPO grew $154bn q/q to $2.48tn, and was up 106% suggesting AI demand continues to expand.
  * We adjust '26/'27 capex to $636/$908bn (-2%/+2%) as mgmt. teams suggest continued capacity investment in 2027.

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Another strong Q with growth accelerating to 56%

Big-4 IaaS/PaaS sales grew 56%E y/y to $112.0bn, a 6ppt accel vs. 2Q and above
our 52% estimate into results. GCP and Azure drove the most revenue upside,
while AWS had strongest q/q backlog growth. Capex outlooks for 2026 didn't
materially change, but outlooks for 2027 continue to suggest significant
increases, and we now estimate 2027 big-4 capex at $908bn, up 43% y/y. Our
three takeaways for 3Q: (1) capacity supply, not demand, continues to be top
driver of growth; (2) most hyperscalers are now planning custom silicon sales
(TPUs, Trainium, Maia 300); and (3) growing backlog (added $154bn q/q to
$2.48tn) supports extended capex builds through 2028. We expect industry
growth to accelerate to 61% in 4Q and continue to favor hyperscalers for AI
exposure. We reiterate our Buy ratings on Amazon.com (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT),
Alphabet (GOOG), and Oracle (ORCL).

AWS: backlog expanding faster than revenues

AWS revenues grew 39% y/y (2ppt accel q/q), above the Street at 38% (though
expectations were likely higher). Q/Q dollar growth slowed to $3.8bn (vs.
$4.6bn in 2Q and below peers), but mgmt. was optimistic on revenues, guiding
to 40%+ AWS growth in both 2027 and 2028. Graviton and Trainium had a 20x
increase in commitments, margins held at 39% despite higher depreciation
expenses, and backlog grew $82bn q/q to $578bn. For 2026, we estimate $176bn
in Cloud revs (up 37%) and expect Amazon's big-4 market share to fall to 41%
from 46% in 2025. Next catalyst is re:Invent, which may highlight new Trn
chips, model progress, and AI apps.

Azure: efficiency gains drive 6ppt accel, unlocking growth

Azure growth of 48% y/y beat the Street at 45% and accerelated 6ppts q/q
(actuals and estimates restated on newly reported Azure dollars). Cloud growth
was driven by efficient utilization of existing capacity and deployment of new
chips. While higher token pricing benefits can be volatile, the underlying
growth in Copilot's adoption and performance reflects higher quality revenues
(workload throughput was +50% q/q). Capex is expected to accelerate in 2H FY27
due to delayed capacity delivery and rising component prices. Commercial RPO
was $677bn (down $1bn q/q on seasonality). Mgmt. guided Azure C4Q growth to
49%-50% y/y, above the Street at 45%, and we estimate big-4 market share of
29% for CY'26, down slightly from 31% in CY'25.

GCP: sixth quarter of acceleration as AI position improves

Google Cloud revenues grew 103% y/y, above Street at 93%. We estimate
IaaS/PaaS excluding TPU sales accerelated 5ppts q/q to 92%. Google's full-
stack Cloud position improved over the last 90 days, in our view, with new
Gemini releases and broader TPU distribution deals. Backlog grew $46.8bn q/q
to $561bn, and Cloud margins expanded to 36.2% (vs. Street at 33.7%). The
CY'26 capex guide was unchanged, but management is expecting significant capex
growth next year and we raised FY27 capex estimates to $320bn (+$20bn). For
4Q, we estimate GCP to grow 107% y/y aided by additional SpaceX capacity, and
we expect full year market share to increase to 23% in '26, up from 18% in
'25.

AI Capex: Lower Peak, Scarcer Compute, Longer Runway, Higher
Multiples  
---  
| Industry Overview  
---  
| Equity   |   02 November 2026  
---  
---  
---  
---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Capex cuts could lower peak profit but preserve compute scarcity, extend the AI cycle and support higher multiples over time
  * With $2.5tn+ backlog and surging enterprise adoption, demand looks durable: scarce compute, not excess capacity, is the risk
  * Funding pressure could impose supply discipline; SOX's 10% discount to SPX already reflects doubts about earnings durability

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Capex cuts unwelcome, but could extend the cycle

Market volatility reflects concerns ahead of US Midterms, escalating AI
infrastructure costs, and potential selective capex cuts or project delays.
Our silver lining: if monetizable AI demand remains strong while capacity
growth slows, capex cuts could increase compute scarcity and delay rather than
pull forward the AI peak. Slower supply growth against resilient demand could
lift utilization, support pricing and reduce overbuild risk. The result could
be lower peak earnings, but a longer earnings runway and potentially higher
multiples for chipmakers already valued as if the cycle is ending. We remain
watchful but bullish AI semis across Compute (NVDA, AMD, AVGO), Networking
(MRVL, CRDO), Semicaps (LRCX, KLAC), Memory (MU) and Analog (ADI, TXN)

Solid demand best argument for cycle durability

Recent hyperscaler results underscore resilient AI demand: 1) total long-term
contracted backlog at $2.5Tn+, 2) AWS revenue +39%, Azure +49% and Google AI
revenue 100%+ YoY, 3) AI token volumes +10x YoY despite constrained capacity,
4) Silicon Data Hopper and Blackwell rental rates +33%/+51% YTD, and 5) SpaceX
suggested current spot pricing supports ~1-year GPU breakeven. Demand is
increasingly enterprise-funded, not just VC-funded: Fortune 500 spending on
Amazon Bedrock rose ~7x YoY, while Microsoft customers with >50,000 Copilot
seats increased >8x and daily Copilot users rose 50% QoQ. The 90s dot-com bust
was excess capacity chasing insufficient demand; AI may be structurally
opposite: abundant demand chasing scarce compute.

CY27E cash burn looks ugly, but that may be the peak

Consensus for eight US hyperscalers/neoclouds has FCF burn worsening to
$335bn, or 13% of sales, in CY27E from $128bn, or 6%, in CY26E. But the
funding constraints could impose the supply discipline investors fear is
missing. CY27E could mark peak cash burn, with the deficit narrowing to $77bn,
or 2% of sales, in CY28E, a $258bn improvement. Funding remains the key
debate, but ecosystem FCF provides another potential release valve: projected
FCF for Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron totals ~$577bn in CY27E and >$800bn in
CY28E (at further risk of vendor financing/circularity risks). Tighter capital
could ultimately extend the cycle versus unconstrained spending.

SOX already prices considerable cycle skepticism

Since CY19, the SOX index has traded at 12.5x-30x forward PE multiple, ranging
from a 20% discount to a 40% premium versus SPX. Today, 16.4x represents a 10%
discount, consistent with AI-cycle troughs in CY23-1H26 and only 10pts above
the deepest relative discount since CY19. With SPX valuation and earnings
estimates unchanged, another ~11% SOX decline would reach that historical
discount extreme, leaving relative valuation at its weakest since CY19. The
market therefore appears to be discounting capex risk before the demand data
have cracked. If paying AI demand stays resilient, lower capex could reduce
overbuild, preserve scarcity, extend the EPS cycle and justify higher
multiples, in our opinion.

The magnitude of Friday’s pullback was shocking – and I did not expect it –
but it’s not out of line with the marketing feedback I’ve been sharing over
the past month. I opened my October 18 Weekend note: “Much has already been
written about the recent, painful NDX/SOX pullback (The SOX is down -15.5%
over two weeks), though based on marketing feedback from recent visits with
Gokul Hariharan, Joe Cardoso and (this week) Harlan Sur, it’s not a surprise,
and even once the market catches a bid it’s unclear that Semis/AI will lead
the recovery.” And I opened our Oct 23 Specialist Delivery call by
underscoring: “Investors voiced … concerns loudly in recent dinners, lunches
and marketing events, and sentiment has been overwhelmingly bearish...”



I could say that INTC is likely idiosyncratic, and that in our opinion SNDK
actually sounded good last Thursday night, and instead blame the neoclouds and
CSP results; but that would be to deny the very real investor concerns about
power/shell and funding, with specific concerns broadly set around:



  1. **Will fixed income markets continue to provide capital for the AI buildout.** We’ve spoken _ad nauseum_ about this, including two all-hands calls with KOLs from across our CDS and fixed income teams; they so far haven’t seemed very worried (though with nuance, especially around neoclouds and HY issuance demand): “The underlying fundamentals and construction performance of projects, hyperscalers and the ecosystem in totality have been quite strong. Much of the negative narrative has been around continued investor willingness to lend and the total quantum of credit ultimately available to the space. We continue to think overall capacity is available.” The variable that most worries them is the signal from equity markets (“equity issuance reduces the technical overhang in credit”) so we’ll be keeping a close eye on any changes in view.****
  2. **Will private equity continue to fund AI capex?** Folks continue pointing to this week’s comments from Blackstone President Jon Gray that AI-related exposure is ~7% of the portfolio, as well as the report that AVGO CEO Hock Tan was deeply involved in negotiations to get parties to commit to fund XPV -  including helping banks get “more comfort around the guarantees from Broadcom that will protect them.” This wasn't the only disappointing news in privates late last week. 
  3. **Will equity markets support the build?** (This was a particular concern later in the week as folks started to call into question the ability of listed companies to maintain credit ratings and to borrow). There also remain concerns about where value accrues (to the labs?) 
  4. **Who will pay the bills to warehouse idle chips/components in case of delays in capacity build?**
  5. **Could Democratic victories gubernatorial elections – particularly in Texas and Nevada - derail the AI build?** And do we get a bounce on Wednesday if we avoid strong anti-data center mandates (or does the focus just shift to power availability, ’28 capex and rising costs)? Based on discussions, it seems like 1) a D sweep is now expected and 2) data centers may be overstated as a concern (i.e. not a key issue for most voters) 



It doesn’t help that several recent raises are under water; and a flood of
bearish articles on Friday was coincident with market action, but the main
questions I’ve been getting have centered around the incremental buyer. The
worry is that long only investors are still neutral-to-overweight in
aggregate, so despite having duration they may not yet have demand; that was
my sense during recent marketing. Our Position Intel (i.e. Prime) team’s
Tactical Positioning Monitor is still only flashing NEUTRAL, and team head
John Schlegel had this to say on Friday: “there have been a lot of different
signs of de-risking over the past month, which—taken together—could suggest an
improvement is due soon.  However, the lack of capitulation (at least prior to
today), concerns about escalation in the Middle East post US midterm
elections, and lingering AI concerns do make it hard to have strong conviction
on the path forward.” On the positive side, we’ve seen continued de-grossing
(especially Multi-Strats), and prior -3z events like this saw positive spreads
in 6 of the last 7 cases… though risks include potential Quant de-grossing and
still-elevated US Tech flows/futures positioning. Retail has stayed sidelined
(sentiment at 6th %-tile), ETF flows stayed positive (+1z), and CTA
positioning fell MoM but is only 44th %-tile LT in US equities.



Where to hide? Names that have come up in discussions (several of which I’ve
written about recently): AVGO & NVDA (no more negative discovery value), KLAC
(similar, plus leveraged to rising INTC spend), AAPL (short AI), and NXPI
(cheap and not really AI-levered).
